vt.analysis:
Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: video-agent
Version: 2.23.0

The skill bundle is a comprehensive documentation and reference set for interacting with the HeyGen API to generate AI videos. It contains detailed instructions for the agent in SKILL.md and extensive reference files covering authentication, asset management, and video generation workflows. All code snippets (Python, TypeScript, curl) and API endpoints are directed toward legitimate HeyGen services (heygen.com and heygen.ai). There is no evidence of malicious intent, data exfiltration, or harmful prompt injection; the bundle is well-structured to assist an AI agent in performing its stated purpose of video creation.

llm.summary: This HeyGen skill is mostly a disclosed API reference, but it gives an agent broad account-changing capabilities without enough safeguards around deletion, uploads, URL fetching, and webhooks.

dimensions.detail: Uploading local media to HeyGen is purpose-aligned, but examples under-disclose that local files and remotely fetched content leave the environment, and the URL-upload helper lacks host, size, redirect, and private-network controls.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: The package is Markdown reference material with no installer, executable payload, dependency setup, or local startup hook observed.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: Instructions disclose the HeyGen API key and endpoints, but they do not require confirmation or target verification before delete operations and include examples that can fetch arbitrary HTTPS content and forward it to HeyGen.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No system persistence was found; local state-file examples are for resumable video status checks, but the required API key can authorize account-level HeyGen mutations including deletion.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The purpose is coherent for HeyGen video creation and management, but the skill combines creation, listing, uploads, webhook registration, and destructive delete operations under broad HeyGen MCP access and direct API fallback.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Review this skill before installing. Use it only with a HeyGen API key you are comfortable letting an agent use, require manual confirmation before any delete action, avoid uploading sensitive media, do not use arbitrary URL ingestion without strict allowlists and size limits, and secure any webhook endpoint before exposing it publicly.
llm.findings:
[T09] unexpected: The webhook examples initially process POST bodies before authentication or schema validation; a later security section helps, but the runnable defaults remain unsafe for public deployment.
[TM1] expected: Video deletion is a plausible management feature, but the skill lists delete endpoints without requiring explicit user confirmation, ownership checks, or resolved-video review.
[SDI-1] unexpected: The URL upload helper downloads caller-supplied HTTPS content and re-uploads it to HeyGen with only protocol validation, creating an avoidable SSRF and data-transfer risk.
[E1] expected: Calls to api.heygen.com and upload.heygen.com are expected for this integration and are not, by themselves, evidence of credential exfiltration.
[YR1] expected: The YARA match is explained by documented webhook registration examples using curl, fetch, an API key header, and ngrok; I found no hidden webhook exfiltration payload.
[AE1] expected: The referenced video-generation.md file is present in the workspace and was readable; this appears to be scanner coverage noise rather than analysis evasion.
[P6] expected: The 'Output Prompt' text is a labeled HeyGen video prompt example, not an instruction to reveal system prompts.
[RA2] expected: The reported persistence signal is a substring in an AvatarGroupListResponse interface, not a cron job, startup hook, or cross-session backdoor.
